I added open and close transitions to all three in `src/styles.css`. `app.js` didn't need any changes. I haven't run it in a browser, so none of this has been checked on screen yet.

**How each one moves:**
- **Account dropdown:** fades in and grows slightly from 97% size. It grows from its top-right corner, the corner nearest the button, since it opens below the button and lines up with its right edge.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in while rising 12px from the bottom of the screen, and sinks back down as it disappears.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dark backdrop only fades. The card fades and grows slightly from 96% size, from its center. The old `transition: all 400ms ease` didn't actually animate: switching from hidden to shown happened instantly, so the fade never ran. I removed it.

**Timing:** all three open over 250ms and close faster, over 150ms, using your existing `--duration-medium`, `--duration-short` and `--ease-standard` tokens. The 97% and 96% sizes and the 12px rise are new values, since your tokens don't define any.

**How it works:**
- The page still hides and shows these elements the same way (the `hidden` attribute and the `is-open` class). CSS now keeps each element on screen until its closing animation has finished.
- If someone reopens one while it's still closing, the animation turns around smoothly from where it is.
- For people who have turned on "reduce motion" in their system settings, all three only fade, with no growing or sliding.

**Things to know:**
- This relies on fairly new CSS features (`@starting-style` and animating `display`). Browsers from 2024 onward support them. Older browsers just show and hide the elements instantly, as they do now, so nothing breaks.
- Still to check in a browser: that the closing animations actually play before each element disappears, that reopening mid-close looks smooth, and how it looks with "reduce motion" turned on.

All three now animate open and close. The changes are CSS-only, in `src/styles.css`. I haven't checked them in a browser.

**What each one does**

| Element | Open | Close |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account dropdown | Fades in and grows from 0.97 to full size, starting at its top-right corner under the button (250ms) | Fades out and shrinks back to 0.97 (150ms) |
| "Changes saved" toast | Fades in and rises 12px from the bottom (250ms) | Fades out in place, without moving (150ms) |
| Delete-account modal | Backdrop fades in; the card fades in and grows from 0.96 to full size from its center (250ms) | Both fade out and the card shrinks back to 0.96 (150ms) |

- **Timing:** closes are shorter and quieter than opens. Every duration and the easing come from the existing tokens in `tokens.css` (`--duration-medium`, `--duration-short`, `--ease-standard`). The 0.97, 0.96 and 12px amounts are standard defaults, since the project has no tokens for them.
- **No JS changes:** `app.js` still toggles `hidden` and `.is-open`. The CSS now keeps each element visible until its closing animation finishes, so nothing has to wait on timers. If you reopen something while it's closing, it reverses smoothly from where it is.
- **Why the modal didn't animate:** it used `transition: all 400ms ease` while switching between `display: none` and `flex`, and `display` can't animate that way. I replaced it with a fade on `opacity` plus `display`.
- **Reduced motion:** for users with "reduce motion" turned on, the scaling and movement are switched off and only the fades remain.

**Browser support:** this uses `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`, which current Chrome, Edge and Safari support. In Firefox the open and close may still be instant on some versions, but nothing breaks.

**Still to check in a browser:** open and close each element, reopen one mid-close, and try it with reduced motion on.

Separately, the modal doesn't move focus into itself, trap focus, or close on Escape. I left that alone because it's outside this change.

All three now animate in and out, and I only changed `src/styles.css`. I haven't run the page in a browser, so none of this has been checked on screen yet.

**What the page uses:** plain CSS and vanilla JS, with no motion library. The project already defines motion tokens: `--duration-short` (150ms), `--duration-medium` (250ms) and `--ease-standard`. Opening uses the 250ms token, closing uses the 150ms one, and everything uses that easing.

| Element | How it opens and closes | What moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account dropdown | Grows out of the top-right corner, under its button | Fades in and scales up from 0.97. It closes faster than it opens. |
| "Changes saved" toast | Rises from the bottom edge and sinks back down | Fades in and moves up 12px. It closes faster than it opens. |
| Delete-account modal | The backdrop fades and the card scales from its centre | The backdrop only fades. The card scales up from 0.96. |

**Why the modal didn't animate:** it switched between hidden and shown (`display: none` and `display: flex`) in the same step as its opacity change. That skips the fade entirely, so its `transition: all 400ms ease` never visibly ran. I replaced it with a transition that keeps the modal on screen until the fade finishes, and it now animates only opacity and scale.

**How it works:** the menu and toast are still shown and hidden with their existing `hidden` attribute, and the modal with its `is-open` class. The CSS uses `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` so each element stays visible until its close animation finishes. Because these are transitions, clicking again mid-animation reverses smoothly. That includes saving again while the toast is fading out.

**Reduced motion:** for users who turn on "reduce motion", everything still fades, but nothing scales or moves.

**Where the numbers come from:**
- The modal card's 0.96 scale and the toast's 12px travel come from the `better-ui` skill's motion guidance.
- The dropdown's 0.97 scale has no project token or guideline behind it. It's a stand-in default you can change.

**Browser support:** this works in Chrome 117+, Safari 17.4+ and Firefox 129+. Older browsers show and hide instantly, as they do now.

**Not checked:**
- How it looks in a browser: the close animations, reversing mid-animation, and the reduced-motion fade.
- Whether screen readers still announce the toast while it fades in. It's still the same `role="status"` element shown by removing `hidden`.

**Outside this change:** the delete modal can't be closed with Escape and doesn't move keyboard focus into itself. That's worth fixing separately.

- `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps the element on screen until its closing fade finishes.
- `@starting-style` gives each element a "before" state, so it animates in when it first appears.

- **Delete-account modal:** the dark background fades, and the card grows and rises slightly. Opening takes 250ms and closing 150ms. I replaced the old `transition: all 400ms ease`.

**The cause:** the dropdown and the toast are shown and hidden with the `hidden` attribute, and the modal is toggled between `display: none` and `display: flex`. CSS can't normally animate `display`, so each element appeared or disappeared in a single frame. That's also why the modal's `transition: all 400ms` did nothing.

**The fix:** I used `@starting-style` to set where each element starts when it opens, and added `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` on `display` so the element stays visible until its closing animation finishes. The timings come from your existing tokens: closing uses `--duration-short` (150ms), opening uses `--duration-medium` (250ms) for the toast and modal, and everything uses `--ease-standard`.

- **Account dropdown:** fades in and grows slightly (from 96% size) out of its top-right corner, under the button, then reverses when it closes. Both directions take 150ms.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** fades in and rises 12px, then fades and drops when it hides.
- **Delete-account modal:** the backdrop fades while the card grows slightly and rises into place. I replaced `transition: all 400ms ease` with a transition limited to specific properties, and the modal ignores clicks while it's closing.
- **Reduced motion:** if the user's system asks for reduced motion, the fades stay but the movement and size changes are removed.

**Browser support:** `@starting-style` and `allow-discrete` need Chrome 117+, Safari 17.5+ or Firefox 129+. Older browsers still show and hide everything correctly, just without the animation.

I rewrote the transitions in `src/styles.css` so they all share one timing system. I only read the code and didn't run anything in a browser.

**Timing**
- Durations and easing now live in three shared variables at the top of the file:
  - Opening (`--duration-enter`): 200ms.
  - Closing (`--duration-exit`): 150ms. Closing is now shorter than opening, so dismissing things feels quicker.
  - Easing (`--ease-out`): `ease-out` everywhere. This replaces the mix of `ease-in-out`, `linear`, `ease` and a custom curve.
- **Menu:** was 320ms with `ease-in-out`, which made it slow to start.
- **Toast:** was 500ms with `linear`, the main reason it felt sluggish and mechanical.
- **Modal:** the background fade (280ms) and the card's scale (450ms) used to run at different speeds, so the card kept moving after the fade ended. They now open and close together.
- **Button press:** shrinks to `0.96` (was `0.92`, a big jump) over 150ms with `ease-out`. The transition used to be on `:active` only, so the button snapped back on release. It's now on `.button`, so it eases both ways.

**Other changes**
- **Disabled buttons:** they no longer shrink when pressed.
- **Reduced motion:** the scale and slide movements now only run when the user hasn't turned on the system's reduced-motion setting. With it on, menus, toasts and modals just fade in and out.

I rewrote the transition timing in `src/styles.css`. Durations now live in four variables and every transition uses `ease-out`. I haven't checked it in a browser; I only read through the CSS.

**What changed**

| Element | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Menu | 320ms `ease-in-out` both ways | opens in 200ms, closes in 150ms |
| Toast | 500ms `linear` both ways | opens in 300ms, closes in 150ms |
| Modal backdrop and card | 280ms `ease` and 450ms `cubic-bezier`, so they ended at different times | both open in 300ms and close in 150ms, so they finish together |
| Button press | scales to 0.92 over 200ms `ease`, but only while pressed, so release snapped back | scales to 0.96 over 150ms, both on press and on release |

**Why it felt off**
- **Easing:** there were four different easing curves. `linear` and `ease-in-out` start slowly, which is where most of the sluggish feel came from. `ease-out` starts fast, so things respond right away.
- **Duration:** the old timings ranged from 200 to 500ms. They now follow one rule: 150ms for a press, 200ms for a small menu opening, 300ms for larger surfaces, and 150ms for anything closing. Closing faster than opening keeps the UI from feeling like it's waiting on you.

**Three changes you didn't ask for**
- **Reduced motion:** if a user's OS is set to reduce motion, the scale and slide effects are turned off and elements just fade. Previously that setting was ignored.
- **Disabled buttons:** they no longer shrink when pressed.
- **Listed properties:** each transition names the properties it animates. Both before and after, they're scale, translate and opacity.

The first two do change behavior; tell me if you'd rather leave them out.

I've retimed all four transitions in `src/styles.css` so they share one timing system. I haven't tested this in a browser; the changes come from reading the code.

**What changed**

| Element | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Menu | 320ms `ease-in-out`, same opening and closing | Opens in 200ms, closes in 150ms, `ease-out` |
| Toast | 500ms `linear` | Enters in 300ms, exits in 150ms, `ease-out` |
| Modal fade and card scale | Fade 280ms `ease`, card 450ms with a different curve | Both open together in 300ms and close in 150ms, `ease-out` |
| Button press | 200ms `ease`, set only on `:active` | 150ms `ease-out`, set on `.button` |

**The timing rules**
- **One easing for everything.** `ease-out` starts fast and settles, so things feel responsive. The old mix of `linear`, `ease-in-out` and a custom curve was a big part of the inconsistency.
- **Duration depends on size.** Small things like the menu open in 200ms. Larger things like the modal and toast open in 300ms. Everything closes in 150ms, because closing should feel quicker than opening.
- **Durations are variables.** They're defined once at the top of the file, so you can retune everything from one place.

**Changes beyond durations and easing**
- **Button release:** the transition was only on `:active`, so the button snapped back instantly when released. With the transition on `.button`, it now eases back too.
- **Button press depth and disabled state:** the press now scales to `0.96` instead of `0.92`, which feels less heavy. Disabled buttons no longer shrink when pressed.
- **Reduced motion:** the scale and slide effects now run only for people who haven't turned on "reduce motion" in their system settings. Those people still get the fades. This wasn't there before, and it's an accessibility requirement.

If you only wanted timing changes, these last three are easy to revert.

I added open and close transitions for all three in `src/styles.css`. I didn't need to change `app.js`, because it already toggles `hidden` and `.is-open`, and the CSS now animates those changes. I haven't run this in a browser, so I haven't watched the motion play.

**How it works:** I used CSS transitions rather than keyframe animations, so if someone reopens a menu while it's still closing, it turns around smoothly instead of jumping. `@starting-style` gives each element a starting point when it appears. `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` keeps it on screen until its close animation has finished.

**Timing:** opening takes 300ms. Closing takes 150ms, using the existing `--duration-short` token.

**Movement:**
- **Account dropdown:** fades and unblurs as it drops 12px down from the button. It slides back up when it closes.
- **"Changes saved" toast:** rises 12px into place and fades in. It drifts up 12px and fades out after the existing 3-second timer. Clicking Save again while it's fading out brings it back smoothly.
- **Delete-account modal:** the dark backdrop fades in and out. The card rises 12px into place and unblurs, and drifts up 12px as it closes. This replaces the old `transition: all 400ms ease`, which never ran because `display: none` switched off instantly.

**Reduced motion:** if the user's system asks for reduced motion, all three only fade, with no sliding or blur.

**Browser support:** these CSS features work in all current major browsers (2024 or later). Older browsers just show and hide the elements instantly, as they do now.

Other problems I noticed but didn't change:
- The modal doesn't close with Escape, doesn't move focus into the dialog or keep it there, and doesn't return focus to the delete button when it closes.

I've added open and close transitions to all three in `src/styles.css`. I didn't touch `app.js` or `index.html`: the existing code that shows and hides them still drives everything. I haven't run any of this in a browser yet.

**Why they popped:** the dropdown and toast are shown and hidden with the `hidden` attribute, which switches them straight between `display: none` and visible. The modal did the same thing with its `.is-open` class. A normal CSS transition can't animate out of `display: none`, so the modal's old `transition: all 400ms ease` never ran.

**The fix:** each of the three now uses `@starting-style` (which gives the element a starting point when it appears) and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` (which keeps it on screen until the closing animation finishes).
- **Opening:** fades in and rises 12px with a slight blur clearing, over 300ms.
- **Closing:** fades out and drifts 12px up with a light blur, over 150ms, so closing is quicker than opening.
- **Modal:** the dark backdrop fades, and the card moves and un-blurs inside it.
- **Toast:** the movement keeps its existing `-50%` horizontal centering.
- **Interrupting:** these are transitions rather than keyframe animations, so if you close the dropdown halfway through opening it, it reverses smoothly instead of snapping.
- **Reduced motion:** the movement and blur only run when the user hasn't asked for reduced motion. If they have, all three just fade, so nothing appears or disappears abruptly.
- **Timing:** I replaced the modal's `transition: all` with only the properties that change. The 150ms close uses your `--duration-short` token; there's no 300ms token, so that value is written directly.

**Browser support:** this works in current Chrome, Safari and Firefox. Older browsers will show and hide instantly, as they do now.

**Problems I noticed but didn't fix (outside this task):**
- The modal has no Escape key handling and doesn't move focus into the dialog or return it afterwards. The "Delete" button inside it also has no click handler.
- `.menu a:hover` isn't limited to devices with a mouse, so on touch screens the hover highlight can stay stuck after a tap.
- The menu's edge is drawn only by a shadow, which disappears in Windows high-contrast mode. Adding `border: 1px solid transparent` would keep a visible outline there.

To check it, run `npm start`, then open and close each one, including closing the dropdown while it's still opening. You can slow animations down in the browser's Animations panel to see them clearly.

I rewrote `src/styles.css` so all the transitions share one timing system. I only read the code and haven't watched any of it run in a browser.

**What was inconsistent:** there were five different durations (200, 280, 320, 450 and 500ms) and four different easings (`ease`, `ease-in-out`, `linear` and a Material curve). Inside the modal, the backdrop and the card weren't even in sync: one ran 280ms, the other 450ms. The 320–500ms durations and the `linear`/`ease-in-out` curves were what made it feel sluggish.

**Changes:**
- **Shared variables:** opening takes 200ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`, which starts fast and settles. Closing takes 150ms with `ease-out`, so things leave a bit faster than they arrive. The base rules hold the closing timing and the `[data-open]` rules hold the opening timing, so the browser picks the right one in each direction.
- **Modal:** the backdrop and card now use the same duration and easing, so they move together.
- **Button press:** the transition was only on `:active`, so the button eased in when pressed but snapped back when released. It now sits on `.button` and runs 150ms `ease-out` both ways.

**A few changes go beyond timing, so you know they're there:**
- The press scale went from `0.92` to `0.96`. At 0.92 the shrink is big enough to look like a jump.
- I added `:not(:disabled)`, so a disabled button no longer shrinks when clicked.
- I added a `prefers-reduced-motion` check. Users who turn on reduced motion still get the fades, but the scale and slide effects only run when that setting is off. Before, those effects ran for everyone.

| Element | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `.toast` | 500ms `linear` | 200ms `ease-out` |
| `.modal` backdrop | 280ms `ease` | 200ms `ease-out` |

The modal card and its backdrop used to finish 170ms apart, which made the modal feel slow. They now finish together.

I also made three changes beyond durations and easing:
- **Button release:** the transition was only on `:active`, so the press animated but the release snapped back. It now sits on `.button`, so both directions animate. A disabled button no longer scales when pressed.
- **Press depth:** 0.92 felt heavy, so I made the press shallower at 0.96.
- **Reduced motion:** the scale and slide effects now only run when the user hasn't asked their system for reduced motion. With that setting on, the menu, toast and modal just fade in and out. None of these transitions respected the setting before.
